result:
Both integrate one branch's changes into another; the difference is history shape.

`git merge feature` (on main): creates merge commit with two parents. Existing commits untouched, hashes preserved → true history, non-destructive, safe on shared branches. Cost: non-linear graph, noisy with many merges.

`git rebase main` (on feature): replays your commits one by one onto main's tip → new commits, new hashes, linear history, no merge commit. Cost: rewrites history. Conflicts resolved per replayed commit, not once.

Gotcha: never rebase commits others have pulled → their history diverges from yours, and you need a force push (`--force-with-lease`, not `--force`).

Verdict: rebase local/unpushed work to tidy up before sharing; merge for shared branches and for landing feature into main.
